not Human acceptance or numerical execution evidence. See the centralized

This is the single authority for common circuit assembly, ownership, public
boundaries, completeness, and Plan identity. Physical factory values remain
owned by the [Component Authoring Contract](../component-authoring.qmd).
Rendering is a separate consumer governed by the
[diagram contract](automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd).

## One authority and three assembly scopes {#one-authority-three-scopes}

`CircuitPlan` remains the sole root physical authority. Two child-scope forms
use the same grammar without becoming alternate Plans:

| Scope | Creation | Ownership boundary | Product result |
|---|---|---|---|
| root `CircuitPlan` | `CircuitPlan(id=...)` | complete circuit, Ports, and Run input | one sealable Plan |
| inline `SubsystemPlan` | `scope.subsystem(id=...)` | Plan-owned hierarchy used in this declaration | attached mutable child sealed by its parent |
| Library `CompositePlan` | `CompositePlan(id=id, library=self)` | factory-owned reusable hierarchy | one immutable `ComponentInstance` from `.build()` |

`SubsystemPlan` has no detached constructor or `.build()` path. It is always
created by and attached to its parent. An author may nest inline Subsystems
recursively. A Subsystem is an explicit ownership declaration; SCNSim never
infers one from values, topology, names, modes, geometry, or intended research
use.

A `CompositePlan` is detached only while a Library factory authors it. Its
internal native leaves retain their exact catalog provenance, and `.build()`
publishes only the declared pins, parameters, coordinates, and inductive
branches. A consumer cannot reach through the resulting component to hidden
children.

## Common structured-authoring grammar {#structured-authoring-grammar}

The operations below have one target spelling on `CircuitPlan`,
`SubsystemPlan`, and `CompositePlan`, except where the signatures name a
narrower owner. `AssemblyScope`, `PublicBoundaryScope`, `StructuredEndpoint`,
`LinkEndpoint`, and `ElementUse` are documentation unions, not additional
constructible classes. A `*` marks the keyword-only boundary:

```text
AssemblyScope := CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan | CompositePlan
PublicBoundaryScope := SubsystemPlan | CompositePlan
StructuredEndpoint := BusRef | TapRef | PinRef | GroundRef
LinkEndpoint := BusRef | TapRef | PinRef
ElementUse := ComponentInstance | TwoTerminalUse

AssemblyScope.add(component: ComponentInstance) -> ComponentInstance
AssemblyScope.subsystem(*, id: str) -> SubsystemPlan
AssemblyScope.bus(*, id: str | None = None) -> BusRef
BusRef.tap(*, id: str) -> TapRef
AssemblyScope.series(
    *, id: str, start: StructuredEndpoint,
    elements: tuple[ElementUse, ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> SeriesRef
AssemblyScope.parallel(
    *, id: str, start: StructuredEndpoint,
    branches: tuple[tuple[ElementUse, ...], ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> ParallelRef
AssemblyScope.branch(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
    elements: tuple[ElementUse, ...], end: StructuredEndpoint,
) -> BranchRef
AssemblyScope.link(
    *, id: str, endpoints: tuple[LinkEndpoint, ...],
) -> LinkRef
AssemblyScope.ground_pins(*, pins: tuple[PinRef, ...]) -> None
AssemblyScope.couple_inductive(
    *, id: str, inductor_a: InductiveBranchRef,
    inductor_b: InductiveBranchRef,
    coupling_coefficient: Quantity,
) -> CouplingRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_pin(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
) -> PinRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_coordinate(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
) -> CoordinateRef
PublicBoundaryScope.expose_inductive_branch(
    *, id: str, branch: InductiveBranchRef,
) -> InductiveBranchRef
CompositePlan.expose_parameter(
    *, id: str, parameter: ParameterRef,
) -> ParameterRef
ComponentInstance.between(
    pin_1: PinRef, pin_2: PinRef,
) -> TwoTerminalUse
CircuitPlan.add_port(
    *, id: str, at: BusRef | TapRef,
    role: Literal["terminated", "nonloading_probe"],
    reference_impedance: Quantity,
) -> PortRef
```

IDs are typed and scoped. Added components and inline Subsystems share the
direct-part namespace of their parent. Buses have another namespace, while
series, parallel, branch, link, and coupling declarations share the structure
namespace. Public pins, coordinates, and inductive branches each have separate
exposure namespaces. Ports have a root-only namespace, and tap IDs are unique
within one bus. Those structural-handle identities include occurrence path,
kind, and local ID, so the same spelling may validly name a bus and its public
pin or a bus and its Port. An exposed parameter retains its independent
definitions-collection/local-ID identity. Compiler-assigned anonymous/internal
keys cannot collide with user IDs.

Returned refs are typed, immutable authoring handles; raw strings and foreign
handles do not substitute for them. `ground_pins()` has no ID and returns no
public handle: its call grouping is source provenance, not another structure or
ground domain.

### Register a body, bind its terminals, then choose its structural role

`scope.add(component)` registers one catalog-created body. Registration alone
does not connect it. Terminal completeness and structural use are separate
checks. Before complete-graph preflight, every required native terminal must
be bound.
An ordinary two-terminal native body must also belong to exactly one
`series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` declaration.

An ordinary factory component with exactly two intrinsically distinct declared
pins is itself an `ElementUse`; its factory-defined terminal order supplies
orientation:

```python
capacitor = scope.add(
    components.capacitor(id="coupler", capacitance=6.0 * u.fF)
)
coupling = scope.series(
    id="coupling",
    start=input_bus,
    elements=(capacitor,),
    end=output_bus,
)
```

An already complete Composite occurrence or native multi-terminal body may
instead remain one independent direct peer of its scope. Native multi-terminal
bodies retain their required pin bindings; a Composite may leave public pins
externally open when its internal physical assembly is complete. If its
terminal schema permits structural use, the
author may consume the whole body in exactly one structure. The three built-in
grounded resonators expose `terminal_1` and `terminal_2` on the same intrinsic
Bus. Their internal LC, JJ, or SQUID shunts to ground are unchanged. They are
complete independent Blocks: either or both public pins may remain externally
open and visible. Their intrinsically equivalent pair cannot be used by
`.between()` or as an implicit two-terminal structural use. Floating resonator
pins remain intrinsically distinct. A custom Library retains its own declared
terminal names; this is not a global pin-renaming rule.

For one structural use of a complete multi-terminal body,
`component.between(pin_1, pin_2)` supplies the ordered endpoint pair. It is
optional when that body remains an independent peer and never selects a
preferred physical conductor or numerical priority. Every remaining required
native pin must still be bound; unselected Composite public pins may remain
externally open. An intrinsically equivalent selected pair rejects before
mutation and is rechecked when consumed. Parent-commoned final nets do not
establish intrinsic child equivalence. The body appears once; another pair cannot clone it. CPW and
MTL components retain one ordered multi-terminal electrical model and never
become scalar-equivalent shortcuts.

`series()` and `.between()` state endpoint incidence and authored order. They
do not assert a scalar two-terminal equivalent or equal current through a body
whose complete model includes internal reference shunts. An IDC therefore
retains all three capacitance branches, and CPW/MTL bodies retain complete RLGC
matrices, conductor order, and every remaining terminal binding.

Registration, binding, and structure therefore cannot manufacture a phantom
component, duplicate one body, hide an electrical shortcut, or infer an
engineering group. Two electrically equivalent declarations may retain
different authored structure and therefore need not share Plan or semantic
identity.

Repeated contact with a public terminal is allowed only on its already
declared net. It does not duplicate the native body or let one terminal join
two nets.

### Endpoints, buses, taps, and ground {#buses-taps-and-ground}

Structured operators accept these endpoint types where their signatures allow:

```text
BusRef | TapRef | PinRef | GroundRef
```

A `CoordinateRef` is an analysis selector, not a wiring endpoint. An endpoint
must belong to the current scope or be a public pin of one immediate child.
Hidden child refs, foreign refs, implicit loads, implicit grounding, and
hidden zero-ohm elements fail before Plan seal.

These handles answer different questions:

| Handle | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BusRef` | one authored electrical net inside its owning scope |
| `TapRef` | one explicitly named attachment site on that same bus |
| `PinRef` | a component terminal or a child-scope boundary exposed to its parent |
| `CoordinateRef` | a selector that makes an electrical coordinate available to analysis |

Ordinary wiring may use a `BusRef` directly. A named tap is useful only when
the author needs to identify one attachment independently—for example, to
constrain the presentation order of several contacts on one bus. A tap does
not create another net, and its ID or declaration order is not a layout
instruction. Likewise, a public pin whose ID is `"tap"` remains a `PinRef`;
its spelling does not make it a `TapRef`.

`scope.bus(id=None)` declares one logical net. A named root bus publishes an
`ElectricNodeRef` immediately through `.node`. An anonymous root bus becomes
public only when `add_port()` promotes it to the Port-named coordinate;
accessing `.node` before that declaration fails. A private child bus does not
publish a root coordinate; its owner must use `expose_coordinate()`. Taps
delegate `.node` to their bus and therefore resolve the same eventual
`ElectricNodeRef`, while their attachment handles and drawing anchors remain
distinct. Promotion is an authoring declaration, not a render side effect, and
Plan sealing preserves the handle's resolved meaning. A tap has no coordinate
argument.

`scope.ground` is the `GroundRef` for the single canonical Plan reference. It
is valid only where `series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` accepts a structured
endpoint. It is not a catalog component, another physical ground model, a
`link()` endpoint, or a page-wide drawing rail. Ground glyphs remain local to
the declarations that establish their role.

### Series, parallel, branch, link, and grounding {#structured-operators}

`series()`, `parallel()`, and `branch()` are component-containing assembly
declarations: each establishes real electrical incidence and a readable
authored role. They are not labels applied after arbitrary wiring. By contrast,
`link()` joins existing endpoints directly and contains no component.

`series()` requires at least one `ElementUse`. Electrical order is the tuple
order, and each adjacent pair creates one generated private internal node. A
one-element coupling capacitor is valid. Its start and end cannot silently be
the same endpoint; an intended cycle requires distinct declared junctions and
another explicit path.

When an author needs a public midpoint in a series chain, the midpoint must be
declared first as a bus and the chain split into two structures at that bus.
Compiler-generated private intermediate nodes are not addressable pins or taps.

`parallel()` requires at least two nonempty ordered element tuples. Every
branch shares exactly the same start/end pair and owns distinct internal nodes.
Empty tuples do not mean a short. The returned `.branches` is the immutable
tuple of generated `SeriesRef` handles. Each branch's series order is an
electrical fact; the branch collection itself is electrically unordered.
Declaration order supplies default visual order and may enter authoring
provenance, but a graphical permutation does not change branch membership or
the circuit.

`branch()` uses the same nonempty chain semantics, but `at` must be a declared
`BusRef` or `TapRef`. It states that the chain departs a through-bus without
severing it. This side-branch role enters semantic identity and is not inferred
from the part name or final drawing. A branch may have the same electrical
incidence as a series declaration from that bus; it additionally records the
side-branch role, never current direction. A grounded branch prefers an
outward/down orientation when feasible, but the drawing preference does not
change its electrical meaning.

`link()` declares one direct conductive relation with no component. Its
`endpoints` tuple contains at least two `BusRef`, `TapRef`, or `PinRef` handles;
tuple order conveys neither direction nor layout, and canonical membership uses
the existing typed scoped identities. One N-endpoint link is one authored
zero-wire relation, not a star of invented center branches or a pairwise
clique. It adds and moves no component, consumes no registered body, and cannot
replace a required `series()`, `parallel()`, or `branch()` declaration. There is
no `start=`/`end=` compatibility spelling for the target link API.

A parent may link its own endpoints and public pins of its immediate children.
It may not use a child's private bus or tap, even when a Python variable still
holds that handle. A link can make a parent bus, an exposed child pin, and the
pin's backing private bus one final voltage node without erasing any
owner-local identity. A parent bus is optional when a physical structure can
terminate directly at the public pin.

`link()` rejects a raw `GroundRef`; external grounding has the dedicated
`ground_pins()` operation below. It also rejects an endpoint already equivalent
to ground before that call, duplicate logical endpoints, or a no-op whose every
endpoint already belongs to one pre-call electrical class. Partial overlap is
legal when the declaration safely joins at least two pre-call classes and
reuses existing wire geometry rather than duplicating it. Separate links may
therefore extend one net over time without restating earlier wires.

For ordinary non-ground connection, a link may not merge distinct `BusRef`s
owned by its invoking scope, whether those buses are named or anonymous. A
child's private backing bus does not count as another parent-owned bus. The same
rule detects direct, pin-mediated, tap-mediated, and transitive attempts,
including a later edit inside an inline child that would create a conflict in
the containing Plan. It does not ban legitimate public return pins merely
because their component has more than one terminal.

`ground_pins(pins=(...))` accepts one or more eligible `PinRef`s in the current
scope or on immediate children. It grounds each pin's entire currently
connected net, so one call may explicitly ground several otherwise independent
return nets. Distinct pins on the same previously ungrounded net are valid.
Duplicate logical pins or any pin already equivalent to ground reject the whole
call; no subset is silently accepted. The tuple order and batch boundary are
provenance only and define neither geometry nor separate ground domains.

Connectivity validation uses one zero-wire equivalence relation for buses and
taps, public exposures, links, canonical ground, and structured wire endpoint
incidences. It never unions through an R, L, C, JJ, or transmission-line body,
nor infers a short from a numerical value. Coincident structured endpoints,
model-specific terminal shorts, one-Port-per-final-node, grounded Ports, public
pin membership, and complete child invariants are checked over the affected
enclosing Plan.

Each authoring operation prepares and validates its complete effect before an
atomic commit. A rejection preserves IDs, structures, aliases, body
consumption, public exposures, parameter definitions, revision/cache state,
and the diagnostic source paths of successfully committed declarations; it
adds no diagnostic or provenance history for the rejected attempt. A rejected
structure ID is reusable. A link that was legal when declared may later become
grounded by `ground_pins()` or a structured ground endpoint without being
retroactively reclassified as an invalid historical link.

Incomplete authoring remains legal while the graph is editable.
`CompositePlan.build()`, immutable render capture, and `CircuitRun` sealing
perform complete validation over their ownership boundary. A failed authoring
check leaves that state editable and unsealed; rendering does not seal it.
Atomicity covers SCNSim's authoring state, not arbitrary side effects inside a
user's Python factory. A well-typed ownership, cardinality, stale-ref, or
connectivity violation reports `SCNSimValidationError(stage="authoring")` with
the conflicting endpoints, scope, buses, and earlier path. Wrong endpoint or
container types raise `TypeError`; post-seal mutation raises `PlanSealedError`.

Real graph cycles remain valid when authored as separate junctions and
physical paths.

The target decision boundary is therefore exact:

| Declaration | Outcome |
|---|---|
| one bus plus two immediate-child public pins in one link | one valid N-endpoint zero-wire relation |
| two or more pre-call classes with one already-overlapping endpoint | valid extension when every other invariant holds |
| duplicate logical endpoint, or all endpoints already one class | reject as duplicate or redundant |
| two distinct buses owned by the invoking scope, directly or through pins/taps | reject the complete operation |
| a private child ref, foreign/stale ref, raw ground, Port, coordinate, string, or wrong container | reject without publishing a declaration |
| distinct public return pins, including two already on one ungrounded net, passed to `ground_pins()` | valid explicit grounding when the component and Port invariants hold |
| duplicate or already-grounded pin in a `ground_pins()` batch | reject the complete batch |
| connection that shorts a physical element's endpoints or grounds a Port node | reject the complete operation |

No numerical near-zero rule participates in this matrix. Wires establish
equivalence; physical bodies do not.

### Three local-ground roles {#local-ground-roles}

The target distinguishes three authored responsibilities:

1. **Intrinsic ground.** A subsystem connects a real `series()`, `parallel()`,
   or `branch()` endpoint to its own `scope.ground`. The subsystem itself owns
   that grounding and exposes only the boundaries its parent needs.
2. **Parent-applied ground.** An otherwise ungrounded module exposes an
   ordinary return bus as a public pin. Its parent calls `ground_pins()` on
   that pin. A bus whose ID contains `ground` remains ordinary until this
   explicit operation.
3. **Port load/reference.** `add_port()` supplies its declared load to the
   canonical reference. A Port has no separately wireable ground pin, and its
   graphical ground anchor is not a public electrical handle.

The parent-applied form is deliberately small:

```python
return_pin = child.expose_pin(id="return", at=return_bus)
plan.ground_pins(pins=(return_pin,))
```

All three resolve to the same canonical reference for numerical lowering. The
authoring projection nevertheless preserves the intrinsic branch, the
parent-side ground attachment outside the child boundary, or the Port load at
its authored locality. Several local glyphs therefore do not imply several
electrical grounds, while one multi-pin grounding call does not force a shared
cross-subsystem ground rail.

Every final non-ground alias denotes one solver degree of freedom. Ground
aliases provide no selectable non-reference analytical coordinate. Linking or
grounding creates no implicit `NetworkViewRef`, transform, retained boundary,
or reduction.

## Public boundaries and parameters {#public-boundaries}

Inline and reusable scopes deliberately publish their consumer surface:

```python
terminal = child.expose_pin(id="terminal", at=terminal_bus)
mode = child.expose_coordinate(id="mode", at=terminal_bus)
coil = child.expose_inductive_branch(id="coil", branch=inductor_branch)
```

- `expose_pin()` returns a public wiring `PinRef` for the parent.
- `expose_coordinate()` returns a public analysis `CoordinateRef`.
- `expose_inductive_branch()` returns an oriented branch eligible for explicit
  mutual coupling.

One internal Bus/Tap node may expose several differently named ordinary
public `PinRef`s. Each has its own scoped identity and boundary, but all denote
the same true node; no component, Coordinate, or degree of freedom is added.
For example, `expose_pin(id="plus_1", at=plus_bus)` and
`expose_pin(id="plus_2", at=plus_bus)` publish equivalent ordinary pins without
assigning coupling, probe, input, or output roles. Its bus may still have
several taps. A private named bus is not automatically a root coordinate;
coordinate exposure is explicit. The `.pin(name)`, `.coordinate(name)`, and
`.inductive_branch(name)` accessors return only declared public handles.
Externally commoning two distinct public return pins does not rewrite that
immutable child schema or imply the pins were intrinsically shorted. Distinct
pins on one child are not rejected merely for sharing the external reference;
complete internal topology and model-specific terminal constraints decide
whether that commoning is physically valid.

Parameter definitions are independent of assembly ownership. A scope acquires
a parameter only when a registered physical component field consumes the ref.
A reusable Composite may then publish that already-bound ref:

```python
public_capacitance = composite.expose_parameter(
    id="capacitance", parameter=capacitance
)
```

The built component's `parameter(name)` lookup returns the exact original
public ref; it does not create a definition or mutate its baseline. A primitive
field bound directly to a `ParameterRef` exposes that original ref by field
name, before and after clone/add. A mapped primitive field returns the original
`AffineMap.input` ref with its input units and identity, not the transformed
field value; mapping and physical consumers remain separately captured.
A literal-only field raises `KeyError` on
lookup. Composite lookup still requires explicit `expose_parameter()`.
Compatible factory
slots accept either a fixed `Quantity` or a compatible independent
`ParameterRef`. Adding the part records the real field binding and any declared
fan-out. Parameters are never decorative same-value labels disconnected from
physical leaves, and a parent never selects a hidden child parameter by path
guessing. The [Parameter System contract](parameter-system.qmd) owns
definition identity, Plan adoption, values, spaces, and operation binding.

## Logical Ports remain root-owned {#root-owned-ports}

Only `CircuitPlan` creates logical Ports:

```python
signal_port = plan.add_port(
    id="signal_in",
    at=signal_bus,
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
```

`at` is a root `BusRef` or `TapRef`. The Port binds the existing raw-network
load exactly once and returns a `PortRef` for Direct, HB, and view selection.
`role` remains exactly `"terminated"` or `"nonloading_probe"`; the latter is
eligible for the accepted PTC operation but is not portrayed as already
compensated. Final electrical identity is resolved through buses, taps, public
child exposures, and anonymous-bus promotion: one resulting electric node may
own at most one logical Port even when several handles alias that node. Inline
Subsystems and Library Composites cannot create Ports.

## Inductive coupling remains explicit and nonconductive {#inductive-coupling}

`couple_inductive()` consumes two eligible oriented `InductiveBranchRef`s and
one signed dimensionless coupling coefficient:

```python
mutual = plan.couple_inductive(
    id="mutual",
    inductor_a=left.inductive_branch("coil"),
    inductor_b=right.inductive_branch("coil"),
    coupling_coefficient=-0.12 * u.dimensionless,
)
```

It adds no conductive edge. Branch orientation owns the sign; SCNSim does not
infer it from symbol placement. Existing realizability, reciprocity, and
positive-definite inductance checks remain the physical authority.

## Complete structural examples {#structured-examples}

### Grounded LC and reusable resonator

Engineer Chapter 1 begins with the minimal inline example: one signal bus and
two native elements form an explicit `parallel()` between that bus and
`scope.ground`. The scope binds C to one independent ref, keeps L literal, and
publishes both a parent-facing Pin and an analysis Coordinate at that same
signal bus. A root 6 fF capacitor ends directly at the public child Pin; a
separate root signal bus owns the terminated Port. There is no analysis-only
root bus or zero-component Link on the resonator side. The later 120 fF point
changes the real capacitor field on this same Plan and does not retroactively
make every fixed component value a parameter.

The migration-legacy Library Chapters repeat the same internal grammar in a
Library `CompositePlan` and then consume one public terminal while leaving an
equivalent differently named terminal externally open. The electrical values
may match, but the factory-owned version has different ownership and
provenance. No Plan or semantic digest equality is claimed across the two
authoring sources.

### SQUID, cycles, and mutual coupling

A finite-loop two-junction SQUID uses one direct junction path and one ordered
loop-inductor/junction path. Each Josephson component owns its intrinsic
parallel `Cj` exactly once; an exact zero omits that leaf. The shared public
parameters below fan out to the two real junction bodies rather than acting as
decorative labels:

```python
from scnsim import (
    CircuitPlan,
    ParameterDefinitions,
    ParameterSpec,
    components,
    units as u,
)

inputs = ParameterDefinitions(id="finite_loop_inputs")
josephson_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="josephson_inductance",
    baseline=310.0 * u.pH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.pH),
)
junction_capacitance = inputs.parameter(
    id="junction_capacitance",
    baseline=2.0 * u.fF,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.fF),
)
loop_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="loop_inductance",
    baseline=45.0 * u.pH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.pH),
)
pump_inductance = inputs.parameter(
    id="pump_inductance",
    baseline=1.0 * u.nH,
    spec=ParameterSpec(unit=u.nH),
)
plan = CircuitPlan(id="finite_loop_coupling")

squid = plan.subsystem(id="squid")
j1 = squid.add(
    components.josephson_junction(
        id="j1",
        josephson_inductance=josephson_inductance,
        junction_capacitance=junction_capacitance,
    )
)
j2 = squid.add(
    components.josephson_junction(
        id="j2",
        josephson_inductance=josephson_inductance,
        junction_capacitance=junction_capacitance,
    )
)
loop = squid.add(
    components.inductor(id="loop", inductance=loop_inductance)
)
a = squid.bus(id="a")
b = squid.bus(id="b")
squid.parallel(
    id="finite_loop",
    start=a,
    branches=((j1,), (loop, j2)),
    end=b,
)
squid.expose_pin(id="terminal_1", at=a)
squid.expose_pin(id="terminal_2", at=b)
squid.expose_inductive_branch(
    id="loop",
    branch=loop.inductive_branch("self"),
)

pump = plan.subsystem(id="pump")
pump_coil = pump.add(
    components.inductor(id="coil", inductance=pump_inductance)
)
pump_bus = pump.bus(id="terminal")
pump.branch(
    id="coil_to_ground",
    at=pump_bus,
    elements=(pump_coil,),
    end=pump.ground,
)
pump.expose_pin(id="terminal", at=pump_bus)
pump.expose_inductive_branch(
    id="coil",
    branch=pump_coil.inductive_branch("self"),
)

signal_bus = plan.bus(id="signal")
pump_drive_bus = plan.bus(id="pump_drive")
plan.link(
    id="squid_signal",
    endpoints=(signal_bus, squid.pin("terminal_1")),
)
plan.ground_pins(pins=(squid.pin("terminal_2"),))
plan.link(
    id="pump_terminal",
    endpoints=(pump_drive_bus, pump.pin("terminal")),
)
plan.couple_inductive(
    id="flux_pump",
    inductor_a=squid.inductive_branch("loop"),
    inductor_b=pump.inductive_branch("coil"),
    coupling_coefficient=0.12 * u.dimensionless,
)
```

The `parallel()` call creates the two genuine paths
`a -> J1 -> b` and `a -> L_loop -> J2 -> b`; it does not model two directly
parallel junctions with an unspecified loop. This is a real cycle through
distinct paths. The SQUID's exposed return is grounded by its parent rather
than rewritten as an intrinsic child ground. The outer pump scope is completely
connected before its oriented branch participates in the explicitly
nonconductive mutual relation.
The exact Josephson and DC-SQUID physics remain in the linked component and
Root Knowledge authorities; this contract chooses only structural expression
and does not substitute the negligible-loop effective-cosine model.

### Multi-terminal line

For an N-conductor transmission line, `reference_conductor` is RLGC metadata,
not a public `PinRef`. N=1 has two public signal pins; N>1 has exactly 2N
ordered public signal-conductor pins. One possible structural declaration uses
`.between(...)` to place one selected head/tail pair and binds every remaining
pin explicitly by `link(endpoints=(...))` or a bus. An independent line instead
binds every pin explicitly and omits `.between()`. Either form retains the body,
conductor order, matrix coefficients, and section provenance exactly once.

### Three-subsystem model

Migration-legacy Chapters 13–16 author one `feedline`, one grounded `readout`,
and one `floating` inline Subsystem at the root. The feedline owns two
independent N=1 line sections and public input/tap/output pins. The floating
scope owns one mutual C/L parallel network plus two separate ground branches.
Root capacitors join feedline to readout and readout directly to
`plus_1`/`minus_1`. Equivalent `plus_2`/`minus_2` pins link to the original root
probe buses and coordinates. Root terminated and nonloading-probe Ports retain
their distinct roles.

The quarter-wave readout is explicitly a local lumped approximation, not a
claim of distributed equivalence. The tutorials contain public generic values
only and supply no scientific acceptance or consumer evidence.

## Plan identity and one-declaration lowering {#structured-plan-identity}

The target Plan snapshot preserves, at minimum:

- scoped IDs and recursive ownership;
- operator kind and endpoints;
- ordered series elements and parallel branches;
- bus/tap identities, N-endpoint link membership, public exposures, and final
  zero-wire equivalence;
- canonical-ground membership and parent-applied grounding locations;
- logical Ports and roles;
- component catalog source and parameters; and
- oriented coupling declarations.

Endpoint order within one fixed N-link is canonicalized and does not change
semantic membership. Replacing one N-link by several binary links may preserve
electrical equivalence, but it changes the authored structures and therefore
need not preserve Plan or semantic identities. The batch or tuple order of
`ground_pins()` does not change physical ground membership or diagram digests.

Numerical and diagram lowering consume that one snapshot. Pure
`SchematicComposition`, `SchematicLayout`, Theme, and final geometry remain
outside Plan/request identity. By contrast, declared ownership, order, branch roles, and exposures
are semantic structure. Rewriting a flat circuit into a hierarchy may preserve
electrical values/connectivity while changing Plan and semantic identities.

Adding a differently named public pin changes the declared interface and Plan
identity even when physical fields and node equivalence remain unchanged.
This does not require another identity schema or public authoring API.
Factory-source changes may alter catalog/Plan provenance even when electrical
values are unchanged. Invariance applies only when catalog source and all
physical/structural declarations are fixed.

## Open public boundaries and independent consumers {#independent-consumers}

Inline Subsystems and every built Composite kind may have partially or entirely
externally unbound public pins. Their complete intrinsic nets and public
boundaries remain present. An open boundary is not falsely marked bound and
creates no implicit wire, load, or ground. Ordinary native and complete-line
required pins, internal physical completeness, and model-specific short checks
remain mandatory. Authoring legality does not promise numerical solvability.

The Parameter System, Calculation System, and diagram system are independent
consumers of the shared immutable assembly model, units, and physical values.
Parameter resolution and Calculation must work without importing diagram
modules or successfully rendering a scene. Parameter resolution consumes a
frozen Plan snapshot and ParameterSet using the same physical field validation;
CircuitPlan convenience methods delegate without changing that authority.
Runtime consumes its frozen snapshot directly. Diagram imports and public
reexports are lazy without changing public names. A diagram request, layout,
or failure never changes a Plan, numerical request, or parameter definition.
Compiled diagrams are one-way evidence consumers, not numerical prerequisites.

The [Parameter System](parameter-system.qmd) owns definition/value semantics;
the [Runtime contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd) owns Calculation and Result
semantics; the [diagram contract](automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd)
owns rendering, composition, and independent visual evidence.

## Assembly validation and failure {#assembly-failures}

An individual authoring operation rejects violations knowable at that call,
including:

- a duplicate ID, a body already consumed by another structure, invalid
  operator cardinality, duplicate or coincident endpoints, or a redundant
  link;
- a foreign, private, or stale endpoint; a `CoordinateRef`, `PortRef`, or
  `GroundRef` used in a link; or a link that directly or transitively merges
  two same-scope buses;
- invalid `ground_pins()` cardinality, a non-pin/foreign/private pin, a
  duplicate logical pin, or an already-ground-equivalent pin;
- a duplicate tap ID or public pin ID, or an invalid public exposure;
- a child Port, invalid Port role/load, implicit load/ground, invalid
  multi-terminal pair selection, or ineligible/unoriented/foreign mutual
  coupling.

Incomplete editable authoring is legal between calls. In particular, `add()`
does not fail merely because its new component has not yet been bound or given
a structural role. Complete-graph preflight at `CompositePlan.build()`,
immutable render capture, and `CircuitRun` seal instead reject an unbound
required native terminal, an ordinary two-terminal native body outside exactly one structure,
a multiply consumed body, an incomplete independent Composite or multi-terminal
peer, an incomplete public map or exposure, an unrealizable mutual coupling, or
invalid final grounding and electrical closure.

These well-typed violations use
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="authoring")`, except ordinary Python signature
errors, wrong containers or endpoint types, and strict Enum/type violations
retain `TypeError`. Mutation of a sealed Plan retains `PlanSealedError`. A
failed operation rolls back that operation; a failed complete-graph preflight
leaves the prior graph editable and unsealed. Neither failure creates a partial
declaration or records the rejected attempt in diagnostic source history.
